title: Motor Imagery ataset from Ofner et al 2017
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 15 healthy subjects performing and imagining six different upper limb movements (elbow flexion/extension, forearm supination/pronation, hand open/close) plus rest conditions. Data were collected during both movement execution and motor imagery sessions using 61-channel EEG with low-frequency filtering (0.3-3 Hz). The dataset is designed for brain-computer interface research and neuroprosthetic control applications, with classification accuracies of 55-87% for executed movements and 27-73% for imagined movements.
methods_description: EEG was recorded from 61 channels (g.tec medical engineering hardware) at 512 Hz sampling rate with 0.01-200 Hz bandpass filtering (8th order Chebyshev) and 50 Hz notch filter. Reference electrode at right mastoid, ground at AFz. Subjects performed sustained upper limb movements in one session and kinesthetic motor imagery in another session. Each trial consisted of a fixation cross (0s), visual cue (2s), and sustained movement/imagery execution. Classification used shrinkage LDA with discriminative spatial patterns and source localization (sLORETA).
